decisionsOpen.title: Burn-rate / capital runway plan against R300m
decisionsOpen.decisionForCEO: Approve burn target and capital-top-up trigger thresholds.
decisionsOpen.note: R300m must last 18–30 months through build + licensing road.

brief.summary: R300m must last the build phase plus the SARB licence-application road — indicative 18–30 months. Camille drafts a burn-rate plan with capital-top-up trigger thresholds.
brief.background: Build-only posture (D1) means no live revenue for 18–30 months. R300m is the binding capital constraint. Burn-rate discipline matters more than initially expected. Camille drafts an indicative organisation cost plan against the design organisation: current 19 employees + planned hires (CISO, GC, CHRO, possibly Saskia's deputy / IMS-engineer) + Atlas's M-phase build cost + tooling / cloud cost + external counsel (S5) + insurance / D&O. The plan answers: at what monthly burn does R300m run dry; what is the operating runway; what triggers a capital top-up conversation with the shareholder; what scope-cuts are pre-agreed if burn drifts.

options.label: Approve conservative burn
options.description: Preserve runway through licence-application + 6 months post-licence operation.
options.consequence: Implies aggressive ratio of fixed compensation to equity / LTI (S4); tight scope on optional spend.

options.label: Approve moderate burn
options.description: Runway through licence-application; tighter post-licence cushion.
options.consequence: More headroom on hiring / tooling now; less margin if licence timing slips.

options.label: Approve aggressive burn
options.description: Hire and build at full rate; assume capital top-up before runway-end.
options.consequence: Faster build; depends on shareholder willingness to commit additional capital.

options.label: Modify / defer
options.description: Adjust thresholds or hold pending capital-tranching clarification.

recommendation.reasoning: Build-only's biggest risk is licensing-timeline drift. A conservative burn preserves optionality. Aggressive burn presumes a capital top-up the shareholder may or may not want to make on the bank's preferred timeline.

decisionsOpen.title: Board / NED search timing
decisionsOpen.decisionForCEO: When to start the NED hunt; whether to appoint an Interim Board Chair ahead of full constitution.

brief.summary: NED hunts have long lead times. The latest reasonable start of the NED search is sooner than instinct suggests. Owen drafts a Board-formation roadmap.
brief.background: Interim governance is interim. Board-reserved decisions currently route through CEO + CRO + CFO concurrence — defensible for now, not a permanent posture. Board formation is typically 12+ months out from licence; NED searches typically take 6–12 months given fit-and-proper, conflict-of-interest, and committee-composition considerations. With indicative SARB licensing 18–30 months out, an intentional Board-formation cadence starts now or in the next ~6 months. Owen drafts a Board-formation roadmap that addresses: NED-chair search; AC-chair / RC-chair searches; full Board composition; sequencing relative to the licence timeline.

options.label: Start NED Chair search now
options.description: 12+ month lead; chair leads composition of the rest of the Board.
options.consequence: Earliest credible Board readiness; signals seriousness to regulators and counterparties (soft-franchise positive).

options.label: Start full NED search in 6 months
options.consequence: Board lands at licence application; tight.

options.label: Start in 12 months
options.consequence: Board scrambles to land before licence; risky.

options.label: Appoint Interim Board Chair now, full Board later
options.description: Hybrid: get a chair on board to lead the rest of the search.
options.consequence: Pragmatic; the chair becomes a working partner to Marc on Board composition.

recommendation.stance: Start NED Chair search now; full Board search at 6 months.
recommendation.reasoning: Lead times reward starting early. A NED Chair brought in at the 12+ month horizon can lead the rest of the Board composition with you, which is materially better than a CEO doing it alone. Soft-franchise positive — SA corporates and FIs will engage more readily with a bank that has visible Board composition forming.

decisionsOpen.title: Talent retention scheme through the build
decisionsOpen.trigger: Sade drafts an LTI / equity scheme for the build period
decisionsOpen.decisionForCEO: Approve scheme shape + dilution / cost envelope.

brief.summary: 19 employees + planned hires through 18–30 months of paper-only work need compensation + LTI / equity / mission framing. Sade drafts; you approve scheme shape and dilution / cost envelope.
brief.background: Compensation alone is unlikely to retain talent through a no-revenue build of this length. Equity / long-term-incentive / mission alignment become first-order considerations. Sade (HR systems engineer, on interim under Devon until a CHRO is hired) drafts the framework. The cost envelope is gated on S1 (burn-rate plan). The scheme typically combines: (a) an equity pool with phased vesting tied to milestones (M2-M3 reporting build, M4+, M8 cloud lift, licence application, licence grant, first profitable month); (b) a fixed-comp benchmark against SA-banking levels; (c) a clear narrative on bank ownership, governance, exit / liquidity that makes the equity meaningful.

options.label: Approve scheme + dilution envelope as drafted
options.consequence: Scheme rolls out; offer letters re-issued with the scheme attached.

options.label: Approve with modified dilution
options.description: Adjust the equity pool size or vesting milestones.

options.label: Defer to capital-plan resolution (S1)
options.description: Wait for S1 to land; size scheme against the burn target.
options.consequence: Coherent sequencing; talent retention not addressed in the meantime — risk of attrition.

recommendation.stance: TBD; expect ~5–10% equity pool with milestone vesting.
recommendation.reasoning: Industry-typical for a regulated financial-services build; tighter than SaaS-style 15–20% (regulated entities have less ambiguity in the exit narrative). Phased vesting tied to milestones aligns retention with the build's actual progress.

stakeholders.position: Inherits the scheme; should be consulted on shape if hired before scheme finalised.

decisionsOpen.title: External legal counsel for SARB licence application
decisionsOpen.trigger: Imani recommends 2–3 firms with strengths-and-weaknesses notes

brief.summary: Major-firm external counsel is conventionally engaged 6–9 months ahead of SARB licence application. Imani recommends 2–3 firms with strengths-and-weaknesses notes.
brief.background: Imani is the internal legal-as-code engineer; she runs ECTA execution, master-agreement-as-code, clause libraries, and the legal-entity tree. SARB licence applications conventionally engage a major-firm partner alongside internal counsel for: application drafting (long-form regulatory submissions), regulator engagement and meetings, licence-condition negotiation, and post-grant licence-condition compliance setup. Engagement timing is typically 6–9 months ahead of lodgment. Indicative licence lodgment from today is 12–18 months out, so the engagement decision can wait ~6 months but Imani's recommendation paper can land ahead of the engagement decision.

options.label: Engage now
options.consequence: Earliest start; some retainer cost during pre-application phase; firm becomes a deep partner ahead of application.

options.label: Engage 6 months pre-lodgment
options.consequence: Conventional engagement; firm has time to draft and run regulator meetings; matches Imani's likely recommendation.

options.label: Engage 9 months pre-lodgment
options.description: Conservative timing; firm has full window.
options.consequence: Slightly more cost; full preparation runway.

options.label: No external counsel
options.description: Run application via internal Imani only.
options.consequence: Significantly higher application risk; not market-standard for SA banking licences.

recommendation.stance: Engage 6–9 months ahead of lodgment; let Imani's recommendation paper land first.
recommendation.reasoning: External counsel is essentially required for a credible SARB application. Timing 6–9 months ahead is conventional and well-justified. Decision can wait ~6 months; Imani's recommendation paper can land in the meantime.
